API Reference

PolynomialCovers.Disk — Type
Disk{T}

Closed disk in the complex plane.

Fields

  • center::Complex{T} — center of the disk
  • radius::T — non–negative radius

Notes

The disk represents the closed set

{ z ∈ ℂ : |z - center| ≤ radius }.
source
PolynomialCovers.Fiber — Type
Fiber{T}

Representation of a fiber of a polynomial cover.

Fields

  • P : polynomial cover.
  • xs : vector of points in the domain satisfying P(x) = w.
  • w : value in the codomain over which the fiber is taken.
  • S : bound on the radius containing all critical values.

The structure is mutable because fiber points are updated when transporting the fiber along paths in the codomain.

source
PolynomialCovers.Path — Type
Path{T}

Discrete polygonal path represented as a sequence of vertices.

Field

  • vertices::Vector{Vertex{T}}

A path with n vertices represents n-1 linear segments.

source
PolynomialCovers.PointState — Type
PointState{T}

State of a lifted point during path lifting.

Fields

  • x: current point in the domain
  • w: current image in the codomain

This structure is mutated during lifting algorithms in order to track the current position along the lifted path.

source
PolynomialCovers.PolynomialCover — Type
PolynomialCover{T}

Representation of a polynomial map

P : ℂ → ℂ

given by its coefficients

P(z) = a₀ zⁿ + a₁ zⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + aₙ.

The coefficients are stored in descending order.

Fields

  • coeffs: vector of complex coefficients.

PolynomialCovers.basepoint — Method
basepoint(P; s=3)

Return a basepoint in the codomain outside the critical value disk of the polynomial cover P.

The basepoint is chosen on the positive real axis at radius determined by basepoint_radius.

source
PolynomialCovers.basepoint_initial_loop — Method
basepoint_initial_loop(P; nl=8, s=3)

Construct an initial polygonal loop in the codomain of P.

Steps

  1. choose a basepoint z0 in the domain,
  2. compute its image w0 = P(z0),
  3. construct a regular CCW polygonal loop centered at the origin starting and ending at w0.

Arguments

  • nl ≥ 3: number of polygon edges
  • s: safety parameter used in the basepoint selection

Returns

A Path in the codomain suitable for monodromy lifting.

source
PolynomialCovers.basepoint_radius — Method
basepoint_radius(P; s=3)

Return a radius guaranteeing that the circle |w| = R lies outside the disk containing the critical values of P.

This radius is computed using critical_values_exclusion_radius. The parameter s ≥ 3 inflates the critical value disk to ensure safe lifting paths.

PolynomialCovers.fiber — Method
fiber(P::PolynomialCover{T}; nl::Int=8, s::Real=3, tol::Real=1e-9) -> Fiber

Compute the fiber of a polynomial cover P at a generic basepoint using path lifting along a loop around the "point at infinity" (monodromy). The fiber is constructed by lifting a loop in the codomain that surrounds the disk containing all critical values. This loop generates the monodromy action that reveals all sheets of the covering.

Arguments

  • P::PolynomialCover{T}: The polynomial cover for which to compute the fiber.
  • nl::Int=8: Number of linear segments in the basepoint loop.
  • s::Real=3: Scaling factor for the initial basepoint in the codomain.
  • tol::Real=1e-9: Tolerance for detecting new points and for Newton iterations.

Returns

  • Fiber: A Fiber object containing
    • the polynomial P,
    • the list of points in the fiber,
    • the basepoint in the codomain, and
    • the critical value bound used for lifting.

Description

The function computes the fiber over a basepoint y0 chosen outside the critical value disk. A loop around the "point at infinity" in the codomain is lifted to the domain using monodromy, collecting all preimages of y0. Duplicate points are avoided by a relative tolerance check.

This method guarantees that the returned fiber contains exactly degree(P) points. Errors are raised if the fiber cannot be fully constructed or if any path lifting fails.

Starting from one sheet of the fiber, the algorithm repeatedly lifts the monodromy loop and collects new sheets until the expected number degree(P) is reached.

Example

P = PolynomialCover([1.0, 0.0, -1.0])  # P(z) = z^2 - 1
F = fiber(P; nl=16, s=4, tol=1e-12)
println("Fiber points: ", F)

PolynomialCovers.safe_path_arc — Method
safe_path_arc(u, v, ρ; npoints=6)

Construct a polygonal path from u to v that avoids the disk of radius ρ centered at the origin.

If the straight segment does not intersect the disk, the path is the segment [u, v]. Otherwise, the path detours along a circular arc of radius slightly larger than ρ.

Returns a Path.
